history: Version 1: 33 cases, written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran; both arms passed on their first run.

A Rust negative control that skipped the truncation still passed open-torn-tail-truncated-by-first-append, whose torn tail was a prefix of the row appended after it. Its tail became a longer torn ext/note row, and no outcome changed.

Version 2: 55 cases. Rust migrates an older generation at a write open, so the older-generation limit is removed and limit-older-generation became migrate-header-less, with TypeScript's exact message. An open step's message may hold a {src} placeholder for the source path its src field names, and an open step may be marked outside-domain. The 22 added cases and the changed one were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran; both arms passed on their first run.

Version 3: 61 cases. Rust takes the write lease as TypeScript does, so trees list session.lock, which both harnesses read only by its size, and a step may name a handle, a or b, each its own backend instance over the root. The 6 added cases and the session.lock entries of the existing trees were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran. Both arms passed on their first run.

Version 4: 63 cases. Rust runs the catalog's final check of a migrated log, so outside-domain-final-check became migrate-final-check-turn-order with TypeScript's exact message and no rust override, and 2 cases were added: a final-check refusal of a v0 source and a v2 TOOL_NOT_STARTED repair the final check admits. The changed and added expectations were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran. Both arms passed without any expectation change.

Version 5: 64 cases. Rust writes numbers as JSON.stringify writes them, so encode-fraction-written, a fraction in free data, has no Rust limit, and limit-encode now witnesses the encode limit with a source member spelled 0.0; both were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 6: 69 cases. Rust ports TypeScript's encoding-mismatch refusal, so limit-opposite-encoding became encoding-mismatch-at-open with TypeScript's exact message, and a message may hold a {srcJson} placeholder, the step's src path as JSON.stringify spells it, which a create step may also name. Rust lays out Windows names as TypeScript does on POSIX, so limit-windows-name became three POSIX cases, con, nightly., and aux.txt, created and reopened in both arms, and a win32 case for nightly., the spelling a Windows writer can produce, where Rust keeps the windows-name limit. Two cases were added for the root check: the highest Zstd generation is named, and a flat file is refused first. The changed and added expectations were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 7: 70 cases. Rust reads older-generation rows at any nesting depth, so migrate-v2-deep-tool-schema, a v2 request header whose row nests 207 levels through its MCP tool schema, migrates unchanged in both arms; it was written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 8: 73 cases. Rust ports TypeScript's flat-layout refusal, so the legacy-layout limit is removed: limit-legacy-layout became legacy-layout-flat-file-at-create with TypeScript's exact message, and legacy-layout-before-encoding-mismatch lost its rust override. The root check refuses only a regular file with the flat-layout suffix, as listSessionDirs does, and the id's flat names are probed by opening them, as rejectLegacyFlatArtifact does. session-directory-named-jsonl creates, reopens, and lists a Session directory nightly.jsonl; legacy-probe-finds-session-directory refuses the id nightly beside it at open and create; legacy-layout-file-refused-at-open keeps a flat file refused at open. The changed and added expectations were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 9: 75 cases. Rust holds lone surrogates, so limit-row-json-parser, whose lone-surrogate row follows an issue, became migrate-lone-surrogate-row-ignored with no rust override, and migrate-lone-surrogates-kept, written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran, write-opens a v0 Session whose id and user text hold lone surrogates, laid out as h~D800 and migrated with them written back as JSON.stringify writes them. legacy-layout-noncharacter-path, written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran, names a flat file holding U+FDD0 in the flat-layout message. legacy-layout-noncharacter-path runs on Linux and Win32 only: macOS CI showed APFS refusing a U+FDD0 file name with EILSEQ.

Version 10: 82 cases. Rust ports TypeScript's stored-identity refusal, so the identity limit is removed: limit-identity became identity-path-mismatch and migrate-identity-path lost its override, each with TypeScript's exact message, in which {dst} is the case root joined with the step's dst path, the path the header's id and cwd name. A selected path the header does not name is admitted when realpath resolves both to one file: identity-case-alias-written, on macOS and Windows, writes a log with cwd /w into the project directory --W-- that a case-insensitive volume keeps for /W and reopens it, identity-case-alias-on-case-sensitive-volume refuses that layout on Linux, identity-requested-id-case-alias refuses a requested id ab in Session directory Ab, identity-requested-id-symlinked-session, on POSIX, refuses it through a link ab to Ab, and identity-symlinked-project-alias, on POSIX, admits a log in project directory --real-- whose header names it through the link --w--. identity-symlinked-root and identity-moved-root reopen a log through a symbolic link to its root and after renaming its root, the link-root and move-root steps; the platform darwin and the link seed were added for them, and a tree lists a symbolic link as <link to target>. The changed and added expectations were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran. identity-requested-id-symlinked-session runs on Linux only: macOS CI showed its link ab and target Ab colliding on a case-insensitive volume.

Version 11: 87 cases. Rust ports the released v2 codec's recovery and runs the v0 and v1 decoder's finish after the rows stream, so the `migration/v2-codec-recovery` limit is removed: limit-v2-codec-recovery lost its rust override and became migrate-v2-codec-gap-rethrown-at-turn-end, with its TypeScript outcome unchanged. migrate-v2-codec-decode-issue-rethrown-at-turn-end, migrate-v2-undecoded-turn-end-issue-kept-until-finish, migrate-v2-end-seed-data-thrown-while-recovering, migrate-v0-seed-length-exceeds-events-at-decoder-finish, and migrate-v0-history-refusal-before-decoder-finish were written from the TypeScript sources before either harness ran.

Version 12: 109 cases. Rust ports the Zstd write path, so a case may name compression zstd, which both harnesses configure, a seed may give a file's bytes as hex, and a tree lists a file that is not UTF-8 as <hex BYTES>; the oracle says so, and no earlier case changed. Added 22 Zstd cases: create, flush, and append writing the header line and each batch as one checksummed frame, a first batch publishing both frames; a reopened log appending a frame; the encoding-mismatch refusal of a plain generation at create and open, naming the highest; a torn final frame whose complete rows are recovered, kept by a flush and by a refused contiguity check, and repaired by the first append, which truncates the torn frame, writes the recovered rows re-encoded as eventLines writes them as one frame, then the batch, even when the batch is then refused while it is encoded; a torn frame recovering nothing; corrupt frames, complete frames ending inside a record, a header frame holding two records, and plain bytes under the Zstd name, each refused with TypeScript's corruption message; create over a Zstd log; and Zstd v0, v1, and v2 sources, a torn one and one with a corrupt body frame, migrated to session.v3.jsonl.zstd. The seeds' frames were written by the backend's own compressZstdFrame, and every expected outcome and tree was recorded from the TypeScript backend over those seeds before the Rust arm ran; each was checked against the TypeScript sources (encodeMaterialization, encodeEventBatch, readZstdPrefix, persistContiguous, decodeStreamingMigration, writeSyncedTemp).
